clue.text: Wobbly chap short of power has to get well, escape terrible death

indicators.note: something wobbly is unsteady and out of shape, so the letters that follow are thrown into a new order
short of says a letter is missing from the word chap

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics
taken as written, as anagram material

explanation.surface: An unsteady man, lacking strength, must recover if he is to avoid a dreadful end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of' removes P from CHAP, leaving CHA; 'Wobbly' then shuffles CHA with HASTOGETWELL into the fifteen letters of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means narrowly avoiding hanging, and by extension escaping any grim fate at the last moment.

clue.text: A wedge brought back to secure resting place for gun

indicators.note: to secure means one piece holds another fast inside it
brought back says the pair of pieces just named is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a gib is a wedge-shaped metal piece or bolt used in machinery
a berth is a bunk or a place where a ship rests at anchor

explanation.surface: Someone reverses a wedge to hold a mounting in place for a heavy weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns the A and the wedge together, and 'to secure' holds the resting place in the middle. A gib is a machinist's wedge, not an everyday word.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the nickname for a huge German howitzer used in the First World War, an example of a gun.

clue.text: Bird in building not hard to find by lake

indicators.note: not says the following letter is to be left out of the building word

parts.note: a house is a building
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher says a bird living in a soft structure can be found next to the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes the hard letter from the building. British solvers may think of the river Ouse, which is apt but beside the point.
explanation.definitionFit: The ousel, or ouzel, is an old name for the blackbird, and also the ring ouzel, so it is a kind of bird.

clue.text: One may have crumbled in game — defeat is reported

definitions.text: One may have crumbled in game

indicators.note: is reported says the word is to be taken as it sounds when spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: to defeat an opponent is to conquer them

explanation.surface: A player's piece fell apart during the match, and news of the loss follows.
explanation.walkthrough: Conkers is a British children's game in which horse chestnuts on strings are swung at each other until one shatters.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse chestnut used in the game is struck until it breaks apart, so it is one that may crumble.

clue.text: One unknown number placed in bag — even or odd number?

indicators.note: placed in means these pieces go inside the catching word

parts.note: to bag something is to catch it, and to net it is the same
the Roman numeral I is one
in algebra n stands for an unknown number
e'en is the poetic contraction of even

explanation.surface: A figure is put into a sack, and someone asks whether a number is even or odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'placed in' sets the one and the unknown inside the bag. 'even' looks like a parity contrast with odd, but it is the poetic contraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Nineteen is not divisible by two, so it is an example of an odd number, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Journalist, one young man who somehow set the world alight

definitions.text: who somehow set the world alight

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the crossword's usual journalist
the Roman numeral I is one
a son is a young male child

explanation.surface: A reporter describes a lad who did something remarkable that excited everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Edison, inventor of a practical electric light bulb, literally lit up the world; 'set the world alight' usually means caused great excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: The American inventor developed the first commercially practical incandescent lamp, bringing electric light to homes everywhere.

clue.text: Ship carrying nob who may appear to be bad-tempered?

definitions.text: who may appear to be bad-tempered?

indicators.note: carrying means the ship holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the usual abbreviation for a ship
nob and napper are both slang for the head

explanation.surface: A vessel has a toff on board who seems rather irritable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nob' looks like a posh person but means the head here. The definition plays on people who snap, and perhaps on photographers making people appear.
explanation.definitionFit: People who snap at others speak sharply, so they look short-tempered, though the word also means photographers or fish.

clue.text: The old man with the twitching is to be pitied

parts.note: pa, like old man, is an informal word for father
taken as written
a tic is a habitual twitching of the muscles

explanation.surface: A father who has developed an involuntary twitch deserves sympathy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pathetic arouses pity or sorrow, so it is deserving of compassion.

clue.text: Old scoundrel leading men, one on the podium?

indicators.note: leading means the preceding pieces come in front of the next one

parts.note: a rat is a contemptible, treacherous person
OR, other ranks, means enlisted men as opposed to officers

explanation.surface: A villain of the past is commanding troops from a raised platform.
explanation.definitionFit: A public speaker addresses an audience from a raised stand, so is someone found at the podium.

clue.text: Narrative one acted out

indicators.note: out here means the letters are put out of their order, like a joint out of place

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material

explanation.surface: A story that someone has performed on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acted out' reads as performing a story, but 'out' is the signal to rearrange ONEACTED.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short amusing story about a real event, so it is a kind of narrative.

clue.text: Sex symbol periodical love recalled

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so both pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a mag, magazine, is a periodical publication
love is a score of nothing in tennis, so nil

explanation.surface: A glamorous figure remembers a magazine romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns MAG + NIL into the answer. 'Sex symbol' suggests a pin-up but is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hinduism the lingam is a phallic emblem of the god Shiva, a symbol of generative power.

clue.text: Frolic returning to entertain a village

indicators.note: to entertain is to host, so the reversed word holds the next letter inside
returning says the frolic word comes back, read in reverse

parts.note: a lark is a bit of fun or a frolic

explanation.surface: A frolic going home to amuse the residents of a small settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns LARK into KRAL, and 'to entertain' places A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: In southern Africa a kraal is a traditional enclosed settlement of huts, a rural village.

clue.text: What ship's captain may do to become front-line performer

definitions.meaning: a captain might be in command of, or head, a large passenger vessel
the star act on a bill, appearing at the top of the programme

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition splits the answer into two words: a verb meaning lead and a big passenger ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The top act on a bill is billed above the others, the principal performer at the front of the line-up.

clue.text: Act ruthlessly, keeping bird numbers down?

definitions.meaning: to show no mercy, deal harshly with opponents
bird is British slang for a prison sentence, so this means keeping the jail population low by capturing nobody

explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' looks ornithological but is rhyming slang (birdlime = time) for a prison term.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means acting without mercy, killing rather than capturing defeated enemies in battle.

clue.text: Room like a square-sided box, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word is identified from how it is spoken

parts.note: shaped like a cube is the adjective cubical

explanation.surface: A small room appears to be shaped like a cube, judging from what someone says.
explanation.definitionFit: A cubicle is a small partitioned compartment, such as a changing booth or office space, so a small room.

clue.text: Small city manifesting the foreign spirit

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
gin is a spirit, the distilled drink

explanation.surface: A little town where everyone shows a strange, alien attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: Elgin is a small cathedral city in Moray, north-east Scotland. 'spirit' suggests mood but is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: This town in northern Scotland has a ruined cathedral, which traditionally earned it city status despite its modest size.

clue.text: The soldiers must come to the front as a consequence

parts.note: taken as written
RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British Army corps of soldiers
fore means the front part, as in to the fore

explanation.surface: An order that the troops must advance to the front line as a result.
explanation.definitionFit: This adverb introduces a logical conclusion, meaning for that reason or hence.

clue.text: African shelter built on radioactive element

indicators.note: built on means the shelter sits on top of the next piece in this down entry

parts.note: a hut is a simple shelter
U is the chemical symbol for uranium, a radioactive element

explanation.surface: A hut in Africa constructed upon a uranium deposit.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hutu are a Bantu-speaking people of Rwanda and Burundi, so a member is an African.

clue.text: It could make treading tricky?

indicators.note: tricky suggests the letters of the word given are juggled into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material

explanation.surface: A slope might make walking difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition and also the wordplay: 'tricky' rearranges TREADING.
explanation.definitionFit: A steep slope makes walking hard, so the whole clue describes an incline as well as spelling it.

clue.text: Escaped ducks found in London school

indicators.note: found in means the ducks are located inside the school

parts.note: the LSE is the London School of Economics
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so two zeros give OO

explanation.surface: Some ducks that got away are discovered inside a London college.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal that has escaped is on the loose, free from restraint.

clue.text: Most offensive incident on street started by former pupil

indicators.note: started by says the former pupil comes at the very start of the rest
on in a down entry means the incident sits above, so before, the street

parts.note: OB, old boy, is a former pupil of a school
a scene is a public fuss or embarrassing incident

explanation.surface: An ex-schoolboy starts a disturbance out on the road that is thoroughly shocking.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of obscene, meaning offensive to decency, so the most offensive of all.

clue.text: Deity saying nothing, almost useless

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is left off

parts.note: someone saying nothing is silent
u/s, unserviceable, is military slang for useless

explanation.surface: A god who keeps quiet is nearly good for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops T from SILENT; US is the abbreviation u/s for unserviceable.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Silenus is a woodland god, companion and tutor of Dionysus, so a minor deity.

clue.text: As one saved from flood, daughter being kept ignorant

indicators.note: being kept means the daughter is held within the ark phrase

parts.note: Noah's family and animals survived the Flood by being in the ark

explanation.surface: A girl survives a deluge yet is kept uninformed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being kept' places D inside IN THE ARK, the Biblical refuge of Noah from the Flood.
explanation.definitionFit: To be without knowledge of something is idiomatically to be unenlightened, lacking light on it.

clue.text: Having a liking for character one singer shows

parts.note: a part is a character played by an actor
the Roman numeral I is one
an alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice

explanation.surface: A vocalist reveals a fondness for a particular role.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means fond of or keen on something, expressing a preference.

clue.text: Unusual sight of piano in place for the present

indicators.note: unusual means the letters are made strange by rearranging them

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material
taken as written, as anagram material
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft

explanation.surface: Someone sees a piano in a spot meant to be only temporary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges SIGHTOF into GIFTSHO, and P follows. 'present' looks like the current time but means a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift shop sells items bought as presents, so it is a place for buying a present.

clue.text: Cat maybe with need to get hold of piece of material

indicators.note: to get hold of means the pet word grasps the next piece inside it

parts.note: a cat is one example of a household pet
to lack something is to need it, and a lack is a need

explanation.surface: A cat with a need to grab a scrap of fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get hold of' has the cat-word grasp the need; 'with' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A placket is a slit or opening in a garment, often with a strip of fabric, so a piece of material.

clue.text: Not for the first time assesses comments

parts.note: the prefix re- means again, so not for the first time
a teacher marks work, meaning assesses it

explanation.surface: A teacher grades work again and adds observations.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarks are spoken or written observations, the same as comments made on something.

clue.text: Name of poet using some bawdy language

indicators.note: using some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A poet who is known for using rude words now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Dylan Thomas was a Welsh poet famed for colourful language and a bawdy streak.
explanation.definitionFit: The first name of the Welsh poet Thomas, author of Under Milk Wood, so a poet's name.

clue.text: Information about artistic style

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
re means about or concerning, as in letters

explanation.surface: Details concerning a particular type of art.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre is a category or style of artistic work, such as a type of film or painting.

clue.text: Holiday island has one brief party coming up

indicators.note: coming up in a down entry means the pieces are read from the bottom upward

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
Lab is the short form of Labour, a political party

explanation.surface: A resort island hosts a short celebration soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief party' suggests a short do but means Lab, short for the UK Labour Party; 'coming up' turns I + LAB.
explanation.definitionFit: Bali is an Indonesian island popular with tourists, so a holiday destination island.
